newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Waterford Wedgwood says H1 trading mixed.
newsitem.headline: Waterford Wedgwood says H1 trading mixed.

text.p: Waterford Wedgwood Plc said that first-half trading was characterised by significant growth in the U.S., Japan and Ireland but slower growth in Britain and more difficult conditions in the rest of western Europe.
But the crystal, fine china and tableware group said on Wednesday that despite some difficult markets, first-half sales rose by eight percent to 163.2 million Irish pounds.

"Our overall marketing strategy is proving to be globally successful and the international reach of our brands enables the group to cope more easily with localised fluctuations in demand," the company said in its half-year results statement.
Chairman Tony O'Reilly said the group continued to concentrate on a new growth strategy outlined earlier this year and aimed at doubling the company's size by the year 2000.

He said the group would consolidate its position of leadership in the tabletop industry through organic growth, the strength of its brands, investment to keep it globally competitive and acquisitions should suitable opportunities arise.
Waterford Wedgwood announced a 28 percent increase in half-year pre-tax profit to 9.5 million Irish pounds.
On a divisional basis, Waterford Crystal reported a 13 percent increase in operating profit to 5.1 million Irish pounds in the first half, on sales of 61.5 million.
The margin weakened slightly, reflecting the inclusion of Stuart Crystal for the first time.

At the Wedgwood china division, first-half operating profits rose by 13 percent to 6.3 million Irish pounds, the highest level for six years, although sales slipped to 101.7 million punts from 104 million a year earlier.
"Measured in sterling and at constant exchange rates, sales overall were up four percent on 1995," Waterford Wedgwood said.
The group said sales in the Japanese market continued to surge ahead, rising 18 percent to record levels in the first half.
"Other Far East markets, while still small, are showing great promise, increasing by 69 percent over the comparative period," the company said.
